## Context

When a ticket records no `file_impact`, attestation currency falls back to invalidating on ANY code-SHA change — a deliberate fail-safe, but measured to over-trigger badly: 307 of 1,457 full-LLM plan re-reviews (21%) ran on byte-identical material fingerprints, 171 of them triggered by base-SHA drift alone (analysis ticket b902-18af-14ed-4da1). Allowing drift without re-review and requiring file_impact universally are both rejected; the approved design scopes the fail-safe instead.

## Plan (approved components a + b)

This design EXTENDS the shipped ADR-0002 content-addressed currency machinery — it does not add a parallel trigger. ADR 0002 already scopes invalidation to per-path content hashes of file_impact ∪ cited files; the gap is only the NO-file-impact case, which today falls back to invalidate-on-any-SHA-change. It is also disjoint from the Pass-3 DRIFT floor (bug 5e40, `drift_floor.py`), which governs finding-level novelty WITHIN a review; this ticket governs attestation currency BETWEEN reviews — the plan cites both to pin the boundary.

(a) **Record the review's read-set INSIDE the signed material.** The agentic passes already observe which repository files they open (`distinct_fetches` in telemetry). Persist that read-set (repo-relative paths only) as part of the ATTESTATION MANIFEST that `sign` covers (alongside `verified_at_sha`), not merely the unsigned sidecar: a tampered or truncated read-set then fails signature verification, which resolves to the fail-safe (invalidate). An unsigned copy may also ride in the sidecar for observability, but currency evaluation reads only the signed manifest.

(b) **Feed the read-set into the ADR-0002 dependency set.** For a ticket with no `file_impact`, the content-addressed dependency set becomes read-set ∪ plan-cited paths ∪ the fixed blast-radius globs, evaluated by the SAME per-path content-hash currency check ADR 0002 already ships (no new diff walker; `git diff --name-only` is only the optimization ADR 0002 already uses). The blast-radius globs are named concretely: `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria/**`, `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/*.md`, `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/*.yaml`, `.rebar/criteria_routing.json`, and `rebar.toml`. Empty dependency set (review read nothing, cited nothing) → only the blast-radius globs guard currency. Missing/unverifiable read-set (pre-change attestations, signature mismatch, diff failure) → today's invalidate-on-any-change. The fail-safe is never weaker than the status quo.

A review that read no code and cites no code (a genuinely no-code ticket) has an empty basis and stops re-triggering on unrelated code motion — the original complaint — while a review that DID consult code is invalidated exactly when consulted or cited material moves.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The signed attestation manifest records the agentic passes' distinct repository read paths for reviews where any agentic pass ran (absent/empty otherwise), and signature verification fails on a modified read-set. Verify: `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit -k "attest and read_set" -x` passes with new tests pinning the field and the tamper case.
- [ ] With no file_impact recorded and a moved SHA, currency evaluation reuses the ADR-0002 content-hash check over read-set ∪ cited paths ∪ the named blast-radius globs; an untouched dependency set leaves the attestation current, a touched path invalidates. Verify: unit tests cover both directions through the existing ADR-0002 seam (no parallel code path).
- [ ] Tampered/unverifiable read-set, pre-change attestations lacking the field, and content-hash computation failure each fall back to invalidate (fail-safe preserved). Verify: unit tests cover each fallback.
- [ ] `rebar review-plan <id> --status` reports which basis (file_impact | read-set | fail-safe) currency was decided on. Verify: CLI output assertion in tests.
